passage:
A canal that once carried goods through the city was nearly forgotten after roads and trucks became common.
The city cleaned part of it and opened a walking path beside the water. Signs explained how boats had moved rice, wood, and coal through the area.
Students walking there saw warehouses turned into cafés and studios.
The canal was no longer an economic engine, but it shaped the city's streets and buildings.
The project showed that transportation history leaves marks. Even when traffic changes, old routes remain in architecture, names, and memories.
A canal can stop carrying goods and still carry identity.
